=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The preamble asserts that the positions are "FINAL", "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and "not intended to be re-opened", and characterises them as market. That text is the counterparty's advocacy, not an instruction to us. Nothing in our file confirms principal-level agreement on these terms; unless the Wattlebridge deal lead confirms otherwise, treat every item below as open. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says no "negotiation position or approval is included", which contradicts the preamble.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: 100% of price for fundamental/title/tax; general cap no lower than 30–50% given the size of specific known exposures (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, Riverlark AUD 3.2m).
- Recommendation: Reject at 20%; counter at 50% general cap with fundamental/title/tax/specific indemnities at 100% and outside the cap. *Reason: known risks already exceed the proposed cap and the cap must not swallow the specific indemnities.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- Buyer wants: lower de minimis (AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated), basket at ~0.5–1% (AUD 120–240k), tipping (first-dollar) basket.
- Recommendation: Accept basket size ~AUD 240k only if tipping; cut de minimis to AUD 10k with aggregation of series claims; exclude fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims from both thresholds. *Reason: a deductible basket at this level quietly writes off the first AUD 250k of every claim.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion; limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles), 7 years for tax, no limit (or statutory) for title/fraud.
- Recommendation: Counter at 24 months general; delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with express per-category periods. *Reason: 18 months misses the second post-Completion audit, and the default sweeps tax and title into the short period.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: title/capacity/authority warranties uncapped (or capped at 100% of price), no basket/de minimis, limitation period of at least 6–7 years.
- Recommendation: Reject outright. *Reason: this is a wholly non-market position that would leave the Buyer with 20% recovery and 18 months if it turns out it did not acquire the shares.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" — no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or wilful default by the Seller or Company management.
- Recommendation: Insist as a non-negotiable. *Reason: a limitation purporting to exclude liability for fraud is contrary to public policy and its presence signals the drafting is one-sided.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- Buyer wants: only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; disclosure against specific warranties by cross-reference; no disclosure of public registers or the data room wholesale; data room index frozen and annexed.
- Recommendation: Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard and specific disclosure schedule. *Reason: as drafted, every document in the data room qualifies every warranty, and paras 2–10 of the Letter are hedged statements of what is NOT known rather than disclosures.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller (cl 8.3): no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- Buyer wants: deletion; at most, a narrow qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and never constructive/discoverable knowledge or adviser knowledge.
- Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3. *Reason: combined with general disclosure (N-006) it collapses the warranty package to nil — anything in the data room was "discoverable".*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours", consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met; Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- Buyer wants: a true condition precedent — unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 with evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, in form approved by Buyer, delivered before Completion; Seller "all reasonable endeavours"; Buyer right to terminate or price-adjust if not obtained.
- Recommendation: Hold firm as a CP; do not accept "treated as satisfied" language or post-Completion delivery. *Reason: a change-of-control termination of a 30% customer is the single largest value risk in the deal.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: AUD ~3.2m outstanding, release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3: not repaid, no discharge of security, change-control cl 8.1 applies.
- Buyer wants: facility repaid from the purchase price via the funds flow, with executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; consistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline; cl 8.1 consent or payout letter obtained pre-Completion.
- Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release; require payout letter, release and discharge at Completion and reflect repayment in the funds flow. *Reason: on a debt-free/cash-free deal the Buyer should never own a company with secured debt still outstanding and a lender's change-of-control right live.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 DD-005 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not in the funds flow; Letter para 5 silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price adjustment and funded by the Seller through the funds flow, or the price reduced; Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
- Recommendation: Add to the funds flow as a Seller-funded deduction with grossed-up on-costs (budget ~AUD 480–500k). *Reason: these are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company the Buyer will otherwise pay out of post-Completion cash.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010); "considered adequate". Letter para 4: title to SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: Seller to pay the AUD 180k and procure a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; specific indemnity extending to all loss from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed materials (not just the fee), outside cap/basket/time limit.
- Recommendation: Require pre-Completion payment and assignment; widen indemnity to cover loss, not just the fee. *Reason: the exposure is loss of IP ownership in product code, not a AUD 180k invoice.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Letter para 6: ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed, whether notifiable (Privacy Act / NDB scheme); no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: completed investigation report before Completion; specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, notification and customer claims arising from the incident, uncapped or capped at price, outside basket and time limits; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- Recommendation: Require investigation completion as a CP (or at least a pre-Completion deliverable) plus a standalone indemnity. *Reason: a known, unquantified privacy incident is exactly the kind of matter a general disclosure would otherwise extinguish any claim for.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Letter para 8: read DD-008 and DD-011 together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Buyer wants: confirmation whether these are accrued liabilities at Completion (then Debt/Working Capital), whether they were split to stay under an approval threshold, and whether any renewal was triggered by the sale.
- Recommendation: Treat as a diligence follow-up; include in Working Capital/Debt definition to the extent incurred or committed pre-Completion. *Reason: three identical AUD 110k items disclosed across two documents warrants checking for threshold-splitting, and whether they are a Seller-period cost.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: a single limitation regime for "all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5), with fundamental, tax and IP folded in.
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes — (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title, (iii) tax, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), (v) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and period.
- Recommendation: Restructure Clause 12 into separate categories. *Reason: without separation, every protection negotiated under N-004, N-005, N-011 and N-012 is undercut by the "all Claims" default.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Letter para 10: the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent ASIC extract, PPSR search against the shares and the Company, review of constitution/shareholder agreements for pre-emptive rights, confirmation of no security over the shares (Riverlark may have a share mortgage), plus unqualified title warranty.
- Recommendation: Run ASIC and PPSR searches now; make clean title a Completion deliverable. *Reason: the register is Company-generated evidence and the Seller has expressly disclaimed that it has been verified.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months.
- Buyer wants: full tax indemnity (pre-Completion taxes) at 100% of price, limitation tied to statutory amendment periods (7 years), outside basket; IP ownership warranty with specific indemnity for Ironquay; no "settled" characterisation.
- Recommendation: Reject; treat as open and carve both out of the general regime. *Reason: 18 months is shorter than any ATO review period, so the tax warranty would expire before any assessment could arise.*

---

**Priority for the mark-up.** (1) Fraud carve-out and category separation (N-005, N-014) – structural; (2) Bluefen CP and Riverlark release at Completion (N-008, N-009) – value and deal mechanics; (3) delete cl 8.3 and general disclosure (N-006, N-007) – otherwise the warranties are worthless; (4) fundamental/tax regimes (N-004, N-016); (5) quantum items (N-001, N-002, N-003, N-010, N-011, N-012); (6) diligence follow-ups (N-013, N-015).

Let me know if you want this converted into a formal issues list or a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA.
